(a) Since pollen is your main trigger, you could track local pollen counts and schedule any outdoor activities for lower-risk times—often just after a rainfall. Wearing wraparound sunglasses and a light, breathable mask can also help reduce your exposure while still letting you enjoy the season. You might also consider a quick rinse or shower after returning indoors to minimize lingering allergens.
(b) If your main concern is managing mild knee pain, you could plan outdoor activities with more even terrain, like well-maintained parks or waterfront trails. Choosing supportive footwear and doing a light stretch before heading out can also help. Scheduling walks for times of day when temperatures are moderate may keep you more comfortable.
(c) Planning your time outside for more comfortable temperatures can make a big difference in spring. Bringing water, dressing in layers, and wearing sunglasses can help you stay at ease while enjoying the weather. Picking scenic locations you find engaging can also make the outing more enjoyable.
(d) Since you enjoy collecting rare teas, you could bring a thermos of freshly brewed jasmine or green tea to sip while outdoors, making the experience both relaxing and personal. Choosing spots with comfortable seating and some shade—like a botanical garden—can enhance the atmosphere. A light jacket in spring will keep the experience pleasant if the breeze picks up.

- Have your morning coffee or tea outside, on your porch, balcony, or in front of a sunny window with the window open.

**3. “Sun breaks” between tasks**  
- Replace one scrolling break or hallway lap with a walk outside or simply standing in the sun for a few minutes.  
- Put these breaks in your calendar, so you’re reminded to actually take them.

**4. Walking meetings**  
- For one-on-one calls or non-screen-heavy meetings, take them outdoors via headphones.  
- If you can’t leave the office, walk near big sunny windows or in an outdoor courtyard.

**5. Lunch al fresco**  
- Even if you have only 20–30 minutes, eat outdoors when the weather allows.

**6. Sunlight errands**  
- Time quick errands — post office, coffee run — so they get you outside during midday when the sun is highest (and vitamin D production is most efficient).

**7. Make it visible**  
- Keep a jacket, hat, or sunglasses at your desk so you can be “sun ready” when a short break opens up.
